title: Portfolio website
headline: Your portfolio website plan
example: Build a portfolio website to show my work
starterBrief:
Goal: a portfolio website for [your name], [your role].
Audience: [who should see it, for example hiring managers or clients].
Pages: Home, Work (3 to 5 projects), About, Contact.
Tone: plain, confident, no buzzwords.
Must have: fast on a phone, easy to update, readable in dark mode.
Budget: [your monthly limit].
My experience with websites: [none / some / comfortable with code].
Ask me anything you need before suggesting a design.

simple.summary: Start from a finished template, let {job:ai-assistant} draft your text, and publish with a simple host. You edit words and images; you do not write code.

steps.title: Collect your material
steps.detail: Gather 3 to 5 projects with a photo, a one-line result and a link for each, plus a short bio.

steps.title: Draft the words
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a first version of your about text, then rewrite it in your own voice.
steps.examplePrompt: Write a short about section for my portfolio. I am a [role] who works on [type of work]. Keep it under 80 words and plain.

steps.title: Pick and fill a template
steps.detail: Choose a template from {job:ui-templates} with the pages you listed. Replace every placeholder before you publish.

steps.title: Publish and test
steps.detail: Publish with {job:hosting}, then open the link on your phone and ask a friend to find your contact details.

commonMistakes: Showing ten projects instead of the three you are proudest of.
Leaving template placeholder text in place.
Publishing without checking the page on a phone.
whenToUpgrade: You want custom animation or layout the template cannot do.
You need your own domain name and a contact form.
You keep editing the site every week.

polished.summary: Build with a framework and a ready component kit, add motion where it helps, and publish from a Git repository so each change goes live on its own.
polished.estimatedTime: About 1 to 2 weeks of evenings (rough estimate)

steps.title: Set up the project
steps.detail: Create the repository, start a project with {job:framework} and publish the empty page first so publishing is never a surprise.
steps.examplePrompt: I am making a portfolio with [framework]. List the exact steps to create the project, push it to GitHub and deploy it, for a beginner.

steps.title: Build the layout from components
steps.detail: Add a header, a project grid and a footer from {job:component-library}. Change the colours and type to match you.

steps.title: Write the content
steps.detail: Keep project text in one file so changing a project never means editing layout code. Ask {job:ai-assistant} to tighten your wording.

steps.title: Add motion with restraint
steps.detail: Use {job:animation-library} on the first screen and the project cards only. Test with reduced motion switched on.

steps.title: Publish and check
steps.detail: Deploy with {job:hosting}. Check the page on a phone, with the keyboard only, and in dark mode.

commonMistakes: Adding animation to everything. It slows the page and annoys readers.
Leaving a component kit's default look unchanged, so the site looks like many others.
Skipping alt text and keyboard checks.
whenToUpgrade: You want to edit posts without touching code.
You need a contact form, analytics or a blog.
You want AI help that works across your whole project.

advanced.summary: Own the whole stack: an AI coding assistant, a typed framework, an editing system for content, a form, analytics and a repeatable deploy.
advanced.estimatedTime: About 2 to 4 weeks of evenings (rough estimate)

steps.title: Plan the architecture
steps.detail: Decide pages, data and what is static. Ask {job:ai-assistant} to challenge the plan before you build.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my portfolio plan: [plan]. List the three biggest risks and what I should decide before writing code.

steps.title: Build with an assistant in the editor
steps.detail: Use {job:coding-assistant} for repetitive code, and read every change before you commit it.

steps.title: Connect content
steps.detail: Set up {job:content-management} so projects and posts are edited outside the code.

steps.title: Add form and analytics
steps.detail: Wire {job:contact-form} with spam protection, and add {job:analytics} with a clear note about what you collect.

steps.title: Deploy and monitor
steps.detail: Publish with {job:hosting}. Run an accessibility and speed check, then fix what it finds.

commonMistakes: Building a custom system for content you update twice a year.
Accepting generated code without reading it.
Collecting visitor data without telling visitors.
whenToUpgrade: Traffic or content outgrows free plans.
You want automated tests and checks on each change.
You need a custom domain email address.

title: Study plan
headline: Your 60-day study plan
example: Make a study plan for my upcoming exams
starterBrief:
Goal: prepare for [exam or subject] on [exam date].
Time available: [hours per day] on weekdays, [hours] on weekends.
Where I am now: [topics I know well] and [topics I find hard].
Materials I have: [syllabus, textbook, past papers].
How I learn best: [reading, practice questions, discussion].
Ask me anything you need, then tell me honestly if this goal is realistic.

simple.summary: Use {job:ai-assistant} to turn your syllabus and exam date into a day-by-day plan, and keep your notes in one place with {job:note-taking}.
simple.estimatedTime: An hour to set up, then daily study (rough estimate)

steps.title: Write down the facts
steps.detail: Collect the exam date, the syllabus and how many hours you can really study each day.

steps.title: Ask for a realistic plan
steps.detail: Give {job:ai-assistant} your facts and ask it to be honest if the goal is unrealistic.
steps.examplePrompt: Make a 60-day plan. Tell me honestly if my goal is unrealistic. List the three biggest risks in this plan.

steps.title: Set up your notes
steps.detail: Make one page per topic in {job:note-taking}. Write each note in your own words.

steps.title: Review every week
steps.detail: Once a week, tell the assistant what you finished and ask it to adjust the plan.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is what I finished this week: [list]. Adjust the remaining plan and tell me what to drop first if I am behind.

commonMistakes: Planning more hours than you can really study.
Copying the AI's explanations into notes without understanding them.
whenToUpgrade: You keep forgetting what you studied last week.
You have more material than one chat can hold.
You want practice questions that match your syllabus.
simple.checkTheFacts: AI answers about your subject can be wrong or out of date. Check facts, formulas and dates against your textbook or the official syllabus.

polished.summary: Add active recall: {job:flashcards-and-quizzes} schedules your reviews, {job:note-taking} holds your notes and {job:ai-assistant} builds and adjusts the plan.
polished.estimatedTime: Two hours to set up, then daily study (rough estimate)

steps.title: Build the plan
steps.detail: Give {job:ai-assistant} your syllabus, your dates and your weak topics.
steps.examplePrompt: Make a 60-day plan. Tell me honestly if my goal is unrealistic. List the three biggest risks in this plan.

steps.title: Take notes in your own words
steps.detail: Keep one page per topic in {job:note-taking}. Mark anything you are unsure about.

steps.title: Turn notes into cards
steps.detail: Make question-and-answer cards in {job:flashcards-and-quizzes}. Write the questions yourself where you can.
steps.examplePrompt: Here are my notes on [topic]. Write 10 question-and-answer flashcards. Mark any answer you are unsure about.

steps.title: Test yourself weekly
steps.detail: Ask for a practice quiz on the week's topics, answer without notes, then review the mistakes.

commonMistakes: Making hundreds of cards you never review.
Trusting generated cards without checking them against your book.
whenToUpgrade: You need answers grounded in your own course material.
Your reading list is long and you need to find sources fast.
You want to track progress across several subjects.
polished.checkTheFacts: Generated flashcards and explanations can contain mistakes. Check each one against your textbook or syllabus before you memorise it.

advanced.summary: Ground your study in your own sources: {job:research-with-sources} answers from your material, {job:flashcards-and-quizzes} schedules reviews and {job:ai-assistant} manages the plan.
advanced.estimatedTime: Half a day to set up, then daily study (rough estimate)

steps.title: Load your sources
steps.detail: Add your syllabus, textbook chapters and past papers to {job:research-with-sources}.

steps.title: Plan with the assistant
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a 60-day plan built from the syllabus, and ask it to list the biggest risks.
steps.examplePrompt: Make a 60-day plan. Tell me honestly if my goal is unrealistic. List the three biggest risks in this plan.

steps.title: Study from your sources
steps.detail: Ask questions of your own material and check each answer against the cited page.
steps.examplePrompt: Using only my uploaded material, explain [topic] and point to the page for each claim.

steps.title: Keep notes and cards in step
steps.detail: Write notes in {job:note-taking} and turn the key points into cards in {job:flashcards-and-quizzes}.

steps.title: Run mock tests
steps.detail: Simulate a past paper under time limits, mark it honestly and move weak topics earlier in the plan.

commonMistakes: Believing an answer because it sounds confident, without opening the cited page.
Studying only what the AI summarises and never reading the original.
Skipping timed practice until the last week.
whenToUpgrade: You study several subjects and need one dashboard.
You want a study group to share the same decks and notes.
Free limits stop you in the middle of a session.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Even answers that cite your sources can misread them. Open the cited page and confirm it says what the answer claims.

title: Resume and job search
headline: Your resume and job search plan
example: Improve my resume for a job application
starterBrief:
Goal: a resume and application for [job title] at [type of company].
My background: [education, experience, projects].
The job post: [paste the job description].
Tone: plain and specific, with results where I have them.
Rule: use only facts I give you. Do not invent skills, numbers or employers.
Ask me for anything you are missing before you write.

simple.summary: Build a clean resume from a template in {job:resume-builder}, then ask {job:ai-assistant} to tighten the wording using only facts you give it.

steps.title: List your facts
steps.detail: Write down your education, work, projects and results. Include numbers only when they are true.

steps.title: Choose a template
steps.detail: Use {job:resume-builder} and pick a plain one-page layout.

steps.title: Tighten the wording
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to shorten and sharpen each line, without adding anything.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my resume text: [text]. Tighten each bullet. Do not add any fact, number or skill that I did not give you.

steps.title: Check and export
steps.detail: Read every line aloud, confirm it is true, then export a PDF and test that it opens on a phone.

commonMistakes: Letting AI add skills or numbers you cannot defend in an interview.
Using a fancy layout that is hard to read or copy from.
Sending the same resume for every job.
whenToUpgrade: You apply to different kinds of jobs and need a version for each.
You need a cover letter for each application.
simple.checkTheFacts: Every line on your resume must be true. AI can invent achievements, numbers and skills. Remove anything you could not explain in an interview.

polished.summary: Tailor each application: {job:resume-builder} holds your master resume, {job:ai-assistant} matches it to a job post and {job:writing-and-editing} polishes the final text.
polished.estimatedTime: A weekend for the first set, then an hour per application (rough estimate)

steps.title: Keep a master resume
steps.detail: Store every project and result in one longer document in {job:resume-builder}. Cut it down for each job.

steps.title: Match it to the job post
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} which parts of the post you already meet, and which you do not.
steps.examplePrompt: Compare my resume with this job post. List what matches, what is missing, and what I should not claim. Job post: [paste].

steps.title: Write the cover letter
steps.detail: Draft with {job:ai-assistant}, then edit it in your own voice with {job:writing-and-editing}.

steps.title: Proofread
steps.detail: Run a final check for grammar and tone, and read it aloud once more.

commonMistakes: Copying phrases from the job post that do not describe you.
Sending a cover letter that could belong to anyone.
whenToUpgrade: You are applying to many companies and need to research them quickly.
You are building a portfolio to go with the resume.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check every date, job title, employer name and number against your own records before you send anything.

steps.task: matching your resume to a post

advanced.summary: Run your search like a project: research companies with sources, tailor every application, practise interviews with {job:ai-assistant} and keep everything consistent.
advanced.estimatedTime: A week to set up, then steady weekly effort (rough estimate)

steps.title: Research the company
steps.detail: Use {job:research-with-sources} to learn what the company does, and open the sources it cites.

steps.title: Tailor the resume
steps.detail: Keep your facts in {job:resume-builder}. Adjust emphasis for each role, never the truth.

steps.title: Write and refine
steps.detail: Draft the cover letter with {job:ai-assistant}, then refine tone and clarity with {job:writing-and-editing}.

steps.title: Practise the interview
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to play the interviewer, answer aloud, then ask for honest feedback.
steps.examplePrompt: Act as an interviewer for [job title]. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my answer, then give honest feedback before the next question.

steps.title: Track applications
steps.detail: Keep a simple list of where you applied, when, and what you sent.

commonMistakes: Relying on AI summaries of a company without opening the source.
Losing track of which version of the resume went where.
whenToUpgrade: You need to track many applications across several months.
You want a personal website to show your work.
You want feedback from a real person, such as a mentor.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check company facts such as size, products, news and salaries against the company's own pages. AI summaries of companies are often out of date.

title: Make a video
headline: Your video plan
example: Make a short video from my own footage
starterBrief:
Goal: a [length] video about [topic] for [audience].
Where it will be posted: [YouTube, Instagram, school project].
What I have: [footage, photos, nothing yet].
Style: [talking to camera, voiceover, slides, screen recording].
Rule: use only music, images and voices I have the right to use.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a script outline I can film.

simple.summary: Write a short script with {job:ai-assistant}, record your footage and voice, and cut it together in {job:video-editing}.
simple.estimatedTime: A day for a short video (rough estimate)

steps.title: Decide the one point
steps.detail: Write one sentence about what a viewer should know or feel at the end.

steps.title: Script it
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for an outline and a short script, then rewrite it so it sounds like you.
steps.examplePrompt: Write a 60-second script about [topic] for [audience]. Start with a hook, keep sentences short, and mark where I should show footage.

steps.title: Record
steps.detail: Film in good light and record voice in a quiet room. Use {job:voice-and-audio} if you prefer a recorded or generated voice.

steps.title: Edit
steps.detail: Cut out pauses and mistakes in {job:video-editing}, add captions, and keep the first five seconds strong.

commonMistakes: Starting to film without a script.
Using music you do not have the right to use.
Making the video longer than the idea.
whenToUpgrade: You want custom thumbnails or graphics.
You need a voiceover or subtitles in other languages.
You post often and want a repeatable process.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check facts, names and numbers in your script before you record. Use only music, images and voices you have the right to use, and read each platform's rules.

polished.summary: Add polish: a designed thumbnail in {job:design-tool}, clean audio, captions and an edit that follows your script.
polished.estimatedTime: A weekend for the first video (rough estimate)

steps.title: Plan the structure
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a hook, three key points and a closing line. Cut anything that is not needed.

steps.title: Record clean audio
steps.detail: Clear sound matters more than picture. Record a test, then use {job:voice-and-audio} to remove noise or add a voiceover.

steps.title: Edit to the script
steps.detail: Assemble the story in {job:video-editing}, then add captions and simple titles.

steps.title: Design the thumbnail
steps.detail: Make a simple, readable thumbnail in {job:design-tool}: a clear face or object and a few big words.

steps.title: Publish and learn
steps.detail: Post, then look at where viewers stop watching and fix that in the next video.

commonMistakes: Putting too much text on the thumbnail.
Copying a trending format that does not fit your topic.
whenToUpgrade: You want AI-generated clips or a presenter avatar.
You need professional colour and sound editing.
You make several videos a week.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check every fact in your script against a source. If you use a generated voice or avatar, use only ones you have permission to use, and follow the platform's rules for altered or AI-made content.

advanced.summary: Use AI where it helps: generated clips and images for b-roll, a clean voice track and a pro editor for the final cut.
advanced.estimatedTime: A week for a polished video (rough estimate)

steps.title: Storyboard
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to break the script into scenes, and mark which need real footage and which can be generated.
steps.examplePrompt: Break this script into scenes: [script]. For each scene, say whether it needs real footage, a generated clip or a still image.

steps.title: Generate b-roll
steps.detail: Create short clips with {job:video-generation} and stills with {job:image-generation}. Keep only what looks right.

steps.title: Record and clean the voice
steps.detail: Use {job:voice-and-audio} for recording or a generated voice you have the right to use.

steps.title: Edit the final cut
steps.detail: Combine everything in {job:video-editing}. Match pacing to the script and add captions.

steps.title: Create the thumbnail
steps.detail: Design the thumbnail in {job:design-tool}, and test two versions if you can.

commonMistakes: Using generated clips that look uncanny or misleading.
Not telling viewers when something is AI-made, where the platform requires it.
Spending credits on clips you later cut.
whenToUpgrade: You run out of generation credits regularly.
You work with a team and need shared projects.
You need licences for commercial use.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check each tool's licence for commercial use and each platform's rules on AI-made content. Do not use anyone's face or voice without permission.

title: Build an app
headline: Your app plan
example: Build a simple app without much coding
starterBrief:
Goal: an app that lets [who] do [main task].
Must have: [3 to 5 features], nothing more.
Platform: [web, Android, iPhone].
My experience with code: [none / some / comfortable].
Budget: [your monthly limit].
Rule: never ask me to paste real passwords, keys or customer data.
Ask me anything you need, then suggest the smallest version I can finish in a week.

simple.summary: Describe the app to {job:coding-assistant}, get a working draft you can try, and publish it with {job:hosting}. You test and refine; you do not need to write much code.
simple.estimatedTime: A weekend for a first working version (rough estimate)

steps.title: Shrink the idea
steps.detail: Write the one thing the app must do. Cut everything else for version one.

steps.title: Describe it
steps.detail: Give {job:coding-assistant} a plain description of the screens and what each button does.
steps.examplePrompt: Build a simple [type] app. Screens: [list]. A user can: [actions]. Keep it to one page and tell me what you assumed.

steps.title: Try every feature
steps.detail: Click through each feature yourself. Write down what breaks and ask for fixes one at a time.

steps.title: Publish a test version
steps.detail: Publish with {job:hosting} and share the link with two friends. Ask them to try to break it.

commonMistakes: Asking for ten features at once.
Never testing edge cases such as empty fields.
Pasting real passwords or personal data into an AI tool.
whenToUpgrade: You need to save data between visits.
Different people need their own accounts.
You want to change the code yourself.
simple.checkTheFacts: Generated code can contain security mistakes. Never paste real passwords, keys or customer data into an AI tool, and review sign-in and payment code before real people use it.

steps.task: fixing a bug you cannot find

polished.summary: Choose a standard stack: {job:framework} for the screens, {job:database} for the data and {job:hosting} to publish, with {job:coding-assistant} helping you write and understand the code.

steps.title: Plan the data
steps.detail: List what the app stores and how items relate. Ask {job:ai-assistant} to question your plan before you build.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my app idea: [idea]. List the data it needs to store and the three decisions I should make before writing code.

steps.title: Set up the project
steps.detail: Start with {job:framework} and publish the empty app with {job:hosting} first.

steps.title: Build one feature at a time
steps.detail: Use {job:coding-assistant} to write a feature, read the result, run it, then commit.

steps.title: Connect the data
steps.detail: Store and read data with {job:database}. Test with fake data only.

steps.title: Test and share
steps.detail: Write down five things a user might do wrong, try each, and fix what breaks.

commonMistakes: Skipping version control, so one bad change cannot be undone.
Letting the assistant rewrite large parts of the code at once.
Storing real user data before you understand access rules.
whenToUpgrade: You need sign-in, payments or analytics.
More than a few people use the app.
polished.checkTheFacts: Generated code can contain security mistakes. Never paste real passwords, keys or customer data into an AI tool, and review sign-in and payment code carefully.

advanced.summary: Build a production-minded app: a typed framework, tested components, a database with sign-in, analytics and a repeatable deploy, with {job:coding-assistant} as a reviewer and pair.

steps.title: Write the spec
steps.detail: Describe users, data and rules. Ask {job:ai-assistant} to find gaps and risks.
steps.examplePrompt: Review this app spec: [spec]. List missing cases, security risks and what could go wrong at scale.

steps.title: Scaffold the project
steps.detail: Set up {job:framework} with {job:component-library} and automatic deploys to {job:hosting}.

steps.title: Add data and sign-in
steps.detail: Use {job:database} and {job:authentication}. Check who can read and write each record.

steps.title: Build and review
steps.detail: Ask {job:coding-assistant} to write code and then to review it. Read both, and write tests for important rules.

steps.title: Measure
steps.detail: Add {job:analytics} with a clear note on what you collect, and watch errors after launch.

commonMistakes: Trusting generated sign-in code without a security review.
Having no backups or no way to roll back.
Collecting more user data than you need.
whenToUpgrade: You take payments and need a gateway.
Free tiers limit users, storage or requests.
You need legal pages such as a privacy policy.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Treat generated code as untrusted. Review sign-in, payment and data-access code carefully, and never share real secrets or customer data with an AI tool.

title: Research and reading
headline: Your research and reading plan
example: Research ancient Indian stories and read the originals
starterBrief:
Topic: [what I want to understand, for example ancient Indian stories].
Why: [school, curiosity, writing, a talk].
What I already know: [a little / some].
My reading level and language: [language, level].
Rule: separate what the sources say from your own summary. Name the book, edition and translator for every claim.
Ask me anything you need, then suggest a reading order from easy to hard.

simple.summary: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for an overview and a reading order, then read real texts from {job:source-library} instead of relying on summaries.
simple.estimatedTime: A few evenings to start (rough estimate)

steps.title: Get the map
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for an overview of the topic, the main texts and a beginner-friendly reading order.
steps.examplePrompt: Give me an overview of [topic]. List the main texts, the best order to read them for a beginner, and which parts are most disputed.

steps.title: Find real texts
steps.detail: Look for the texts in {job:source-library}. Note the translator and year for each.

steps.title: Read, then ask
steps.detail: Read a passage yourself first. Then ask {job:ai-assistant} to explain what you did not understand.

steps.title: Keep a short log
steps.detail: After each session write two lines: what you learned and what you want to check.

commonMistakes: Treating an AI retelling as if it were the original text.
Mixing different versions of a story without noticing.
Not noting which edition or translator you read.
whenToUpgrade: You need to check claims across several books.
You want to keep notes that connect ideas.
You are writing something and need citations.
simple.checkTheFacts: AI can retell a story or event with confident but wrong details, and may blend several versions. For ancient texts, name the edition and translator, and check names, dates and quotes against the source text or a scholarly reference.

polished.summary: Add research tools: {job:research-with-sources} finds what scholars say with links, {job:source-library} holds the originals and {job:note-taking} keeps what you learn.
polished.estimatedTime: A few weeks of regular reading (rough estimate)

steps.title: Frame the question
steps.detail: Write one clear question, such as how a story changes between versions. Ask {job:ai-assistant} to sharpen it.

steps.title: Find background
steps.detail: Use {job:research-with-sources} for background and open the sources it links.

steps.title: Read the originals
steps.detail: Get the texts from {job:source-library}. Compare at least two versions or translations.

steps.title: Take linked notes
steps.detail: In {job:note-taking}, write one note per idea and link it to the text and page that supports it.

steps.title: Summarise in your words
steps.detail: Write a short summary, then ask {job:ai-assistant} to point out anything unsupported by your notes.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my summary and my notes: [text]. List every claim in the summary that my notes do not support.

commonMistakes: Quoting an AI answer as if it were a source.
Reading only summaries and never the original.
Losing track of which note came from which book.
whenToUpgrade: You need to work with long PDFs or many sources at once.
You want to be quizzed on what you read.
You are writing a paper and need proper citations.
polished.checkTheFacts: Open each linked source and confirm it says what the answer claims. For ancient texts, check names, dates and quotes against the source or a scholarly reference.

advanced.summary: Treat it as research: ground answers in your own sources with {job:research-with-sources}, compare versions in {job:source-library}, keep linked notes and test yourself on what you read.
advanced.estimatedTime: A month or more of regular work (rough estimate)

steps.title: Collect your sources
steps.detail: Gather the texts from {job:source-library} and scholarly work through {job:research-with-sources}. Record edition and translator for each.

steps.title: Compare versions
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to compare passages from two versions, then check its comparison against the texts.
steps.examplePrompt: Compare these two versions of the same passage: [A] and [B]. List differences in events, names and tone, and quote the exact words for each difference.

steps.title: Build linked notes
steps.detail: In {job:note-taking}, link every claim to its source and page, and mark what is only an interpretation.

steps.title: Test your memory
steps.detail: Make cards in {job:flashcards-and-quizzes} for names, dates and key ideas, and check each card against the source.

steps.title: Write it up
steps.detail: Draft your own account, with every claim tied to a source you opened.

commonMistakes: Letting the AI choose which sources matter.
Citing a source you never opened.
Treating one translation as the only version.
whenToUpgrade: You need to read texts in their original language.
You need help from a librarian, teacher or subject expert.
Your reference collection outgrows simple notes.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Open each cited page. Confirm the quote, the page and the translator. When two sources disagree, report the disagreement instead of picking one silently.

title: Business website
headline: Your business website plan
example: Build a website for my small business
starterBrief:
Business: [what you sell or do], in [city].
Customers: [who they are and how they find you].
Pages: Home, Services or Products, About, Contact.
Must have: [phone and WhatsApp link, map, opening hours, enquiry form].
Tone: friendly, clear, no jargon.
Budget: [your monthly limit].
Rule: do not invent reviews, awards or numbers.
Ask me anything you need, then suggest the simplest site that brings in enquiries.

simple.summary: Use a no-code builder from {job:ui-templates} for the site, let {job:ai-assistant} draft the words, and add an enquiry form with {job:contact-form}.

steps.title: Gather the basics
steps.detail: Collect your services, photos, address, opening hours and contact details in one document.

steps.title: Draft the words
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a first version of your home and services text. Replace anything that is not true.
steps.examplePrompt: Write home page text for a [type of business] in [city]. Use only these facts: [facts]. Keep it plain and friendly. Do not invent reviews, awards or numbers.

steps.title: Pick a template
steps.detail: Choose a template in {job:ui-templates} built for your kind of business and swap in your content.

steps.title: Add a way to reach you
steps.detail: Add {job:contact-form} and a phone or WhatsApp link, and send yourself a test message.

steps.title: Launch and check
steps.detail: Open the site on a phone and ask a customer to find your address and contact details.

commonMistakes: Using stock photos that do not look like your business.
whenToUpgrade: You want to take payments online.
You want to update content without a builder.
You want to see how many visitors you get.
simple.checkTheFacts: Details such as prices, opening hours, GST number, privacy policy and refund terms must be correct for your business. Check legal text with an accountant or lawyer; do not rely on AI-written legal pages.

polished.summary: Design the look in {job:design-tool}, run the site on a template or CMS, and add visitor counts with {job:analytics} so you can see what works.

steps.title: Define the look
steps.detail: Pick two colours, one font and a logo in {job:design-tool}. Keep it consistent across pages.

steps.title: Write the content
steps.detail: Draft pages with {job:ai-assistant} using only your real facts, then edit in your voice.

steps.title: Build on a template
steps.detail: Use {job:ui-templates} for the layout and {job:content-management} so you can change text without help.

steps.title: Add enquiries and analytics
steps.detail: Set up {job:contact-form} and {job:analytics}. Tell visitors what you collect.

steps.title: Test on real devices
steps.detail: Check the site on an old phone and a slow connection, and fix anything that is hard to read.

commonMistakes: Choosing a template for looks, not for the pages you need.
Not telling visitors what analytics collects.
Forgetting to update hours and prices.
whenToUpgrade: You need bookings or a customer login.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check prices, hours, addresses and legal pages. Have an accountant or lawyer review any legal text, and do not publish AI-written terms as they are.

advanced.summary: Build a custom site on a framework with a CMS, a payment gateway for India, analytics and a form, with an AI assistant to speed up the work.

steps.title: Plan pages and data
steps.detail: List pages, products and what the owner must be able to edit. Ask {job:ai-assistant} to find gaps.

steps.title: Build the front end
steps.detail: Use {job:framework} and {job:component-library}, with {job:coding-assistant} helping. Read every change.

steps.title: Connect content
steps.detail: Set up {job:content-management} so the owner can update products and posts.

steps.title: Take payments
steps.detail: Integrate {job:payments-india}. Test with the gateway's test mode before any real payment.

steps.title: Publish and monitor
steps.detail: Deploy to {job:hosting}, add {job:analytics} and {job:contact-form}, and check speed and accessibility.

commonMistakes: Going live with payments before completing the gateway's business checks.
Storing customer data you do not need.
Building a custom admin when a CMS already does the job.
whenToUpgrade: You need inventory, shipping or accounting links.
You outgrow free hosting or form limits.
You need legal advice on selling online.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check payment gateway fees, onboarding requirements, tax rules and legal pages on the official pages and with a professional. Do not rely on AI for legal or tax advice.

title: Presentation
headline: Your presentation plan
example: Make a presentation for my project
starterBrief:
Goal: a [number]-minute presentation on [topic] for [audience].
One thing the audience should remember: [message].
My facts and sources: [list].
Style: [formal, friendly, visual].
Rule: use only facts and numbers I give you, and mark anything you are unsure about.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a slide-by-slide outline.

simple.summary: Outline with {job:ai-assistant}, then build the slides in {job:presentation-maker}. Keep one idea per slide.

steps.title: Decide the message
steps.detail: Write the one thing the audience should remember. Everything else supports it.

steps.title: Outline the slides
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a slide-by-slide outline with one idea per slide.
steps.examplePrompt: Make a [number]-slide outline for a presentation on [topic] for [audience]. One idea per slide. Mark any fact you are unsure about.

steps.title: Build the slides
steps.detail: Use {job:presentation-maker}. Keep text short and use large, readable type.

steps.title: Rehearse aloud
steps.detail: Practise once with a timer and cut anything that runs long.

commonMistakes: Putting full sentences on slides and reading them out.
Using too many fonts and colours.
whenToUpgrade: You need charts or images made for your topic.
You need to back claims with sources.
You want a recorded version with narration.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check every number, quote and chart the AI gave you against a real source before you present it.

polished.summary: Add visual support: images for key slides, a consistent design in {job:design-tool}, and a rehearsed delivery.

steps.title: Outline and trim
steps.detail: Draft with {job:ai-assistant}, then cut the outline by a third.

steps.title: Set the design
steps.detail: Pick one font pair and two colours in {job:design-tool}, and use them on every slide.

steps.title: Add visuals
steps.detail: Create images with {job:image-generation} only where a picture explains something. Label anything generated.

steps.title: Build and rehearse
steps.detail: Assemble in {job:presentation-maker}, then rehearse aloud and prepare for likely questions.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my presentation outline: [outline]. List the five hardest questions the audience might ask and a short honest answer to each.

commonMistakes: Using generated images that do not match your topic.
whenToUpgrade: You need data and sources to be defended.
You present often and need a reusable template.
You want a narrated or video version.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check every figure, name and date on the slides against its original source, and label images that were made with AI.

advanced.summary: Back your claims: gather sources with {job:research-with-sources}, build a polished deck with {job:presentation-maker} and {job:design-tool}, and add narration if needed.

steps.title: Gather evidence
steps.detail: Use {job:research-with-sources} to find sources for each claim and open every link.

steps.title: Structure the argument
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to challenge your outline and point out weak claims.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my outline and my sources: [text]. Which claims are weakly supported? Which sources disagree?

steps.title: Design the deck
steps.detail: Build the master design in {job:design-tool}, then the slides in {job:presentation-maker}.

steps.title: Add visuals and audio
steps.detail: Make images with {job:image-generation} and record narration with {job:voice-and-audio} if the deck will be shared on its own.

steps.title: Rehearse with an audience
steps.detail: Present to one person who will interrupt, and fix the slides where they got lost.

commonMistakes: Citing a source you did not open.
Adding visuals that decorate rather than explain.
Using a generated voice without making that clear to the audience.
whenToUpgrade: You present to large or formal audiences.
You need accessible versions with captions and alt text.
You need a team to edit the deck together.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Open every source and confirm the number or quote. State clearly which images or voices were generated.

title: Pick the right AI for a task
headline: Your AI tool picks
example: Which AI should I use to summarise a PDF?
starterBrief:
Task: [what I want to get done].
What I have: [files, text, nothing yet].
Who it is for: [me, my class, my customers].
Budget: [your monthly limit].
Rule: tell me honestly when AI is not the right tool, and what to check before I trust the result.
Ask me anything you need.

simple.summary: Start with the tool below for your task. Try it on a small piece of real work before you pay for anything.

steps.title: Say the task in one sentence
steps.detail: Write what you want done, what you have, and what a good result looks like.

steps.title: Try the first pick
steps.detail: Use the recommended tool on a small sample, not on your whole project.

steps.title: Check the result
steps.detail: Compare the output with the original. Look for anything invented, missing or out of date.

steps.title: Try an alternative if it fails
steps.detail: Open the other options on a card and try one that fits your reason for switching.

commonMistakes: Paying before you have tried the free option.
Trusting the first answer without checking it.
Sharing private files with a tool you have not read the terms of.
whenToUpgrade: You hit free limits while doing real work.
You need the same task done again and again.
You need a tool that works with your other tools.
simple.checkTheFacts: AI output can be wrong or invented. Check anything that matters against the original or a trusted source.

polished.summary: Pick a tool for each part of the task, test them on the same sample, and keep the one that gives you results you can verify.

steps.title: Split the task
steps.detail: Break the task into parts such as research, drafting and finishing. Each part may need a different tool.

steps.title: Test on one sample
steps.detail: Run the same small sample through the top pick and one alternative.

steps.title: Judge on what matters
steps.detail: Score each result on accuracy, effort saved and whether you can verify it.

steps.title: Keep what works
steps.detail: Keep the winner and note why, so you do not repeat the comparison.

commonMistakes: Choosing by how impressive the output looks rather than how correct it is.
Using several tools where one is enough.
whenToUpgrade: You need the tools to work together.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check any facts, quotes and numbers in the output against the original or a trusted source.

advanced.summary: Combine tools into a repeatable workflow, with a check at each step, and prefer options you can run or move yourself.
advanced.estimatedTime: A few hours to design a workflow (rough estimate)

steps.title: Map the workflow
steps.detail: Write the steps from input to finished result, and mark where a human must check.

steps.title: Choose per step
steps.detail: Pick a tool for each step, favouring ones that export your work in open formats.

steps.title: Add checks
steps.detail: Add a verification step after each AI step: a source check, a test or a second pair of eyes.

steps.title: Review regularly
steps.detail: Tools and limits change. Revisit your choices every few months.

commonMistakes: Building a workflow that depends on one tool's free tier.
Skipping checks because earlier results were good.
Locking your work into a format you cannot export.
whenToUpgrade: Your workflow runs often enough to justify automation.
You handle private or regulated data.
You need guarantees about uptime or data handling.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Treat every AI step as unverified until a check passes. Review each tool's data and privacy terms before you send it anything private.

title: Mobile app
headline: Your mobile app plan
example: I want to build a mobile app for Android and iPhone
synonyms: make an app for my phone
starterBrief:
Goal: a mobile app for [Android, iPhone, both] that [what it does].
Who will use it: [users].
The three screens it must have: [list].
What I can do myself: [no code, a little code, comfortable with code].
Rule: keep the first version to one main thing, and tell me what to cut.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a build order.

simple.summary: Sketch the screens, then let {job:coding-assistant} help you build one screen at a time. Aim for one thing working on your own phone.

steps.title: Decide the one job of the app
steps.detail: Write one sentence: who uses it and what they do in the first minute. Cut everything else for now.

steps.title: Sketch three screens
steps.detail: Draw the screens on paper or in {job:design-tool}. Boxes and labels are enough.

steps.title: Build one screen
steps.detail: Ask {job:coding-assistant} to build a single screen with fake data, and run it on your phone.
steps.examplePrompt: Help me build one screen of a mobile app: [describe]. Use fake data. Explain each file in plain words and what I should run.

steps.title: Add the next screen
steps.detail: Connect the screens one by one. Test on a real phone after each step.

commonMistakes: Starting with ten features instead of one.
Building all screens before running any.
Copying code you do not understand and then being unable to fix it.
whenToUpgrade: You need to save users' data or let them log in.
You want to publish to a store.
You want the app to work on both Android and iPhone.
simple.checkTheFacts: Store rules and fees change. Read the current developer rules for each store before you plan to publish.

steps.task: building one screen at a time

polished.summary: Pick one cross-platform framework, add saved data and login, and test with real people before you publish.

steps.title: Choose a framework
steps.detail: Pick one cross-platform framework with {job:framework} so one codebase covers both phones.

steps.title: Design the flow
steps.detail: Make the main flow in {job:design-tool}: first open, main action, result.

steps.title: Build with data
steps.detail: Store the app's data in {job:database} and build the main flow with {job:coding-assistant}.

steps.title: Add login
steps.detail: Use {job:authentication} instead of writing login yourself.

steps.title: Test with five people
steps.detail: Give the build to five real users and watch where they get stuck.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my app's main flow: [describe]. Write a five-question test script for first-time users and what to watch for.

commonMistakes: Writing login and password storage by hand.
Skipping tests on a real, older phone.
Ignoring what happens with no internet.
whenToUpgrade: You need to measure how people use the app.
You need a team to work on the same code.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check the current store requirements, privacy rules and any fees on the official pages before you publish.

advanced.summary: Add version control, ready-made components, analytics and payments, and treat the first release as an experiment you measure.

steps.title: Set up the project
steps.detail: Create a repository in {job:version-control} and commit after every working step.

steps.title: Use a component kit
steps.detail: Build screens from {job:component-library} so they look consistent and are accessible.

steps.title: Back the app with data and login
steps.detail: Use {job:database} for data and {job:authentication} for accounts. Write down who can read and write what.

steps.title: Measure
steps.detail: Add {job:analytics} for the few events that matter, and say in your privacy text what you collect.

steps.title: Release small
steps.detail: Release to a small group first and fix what they report before a wide launch.

commonMistakes: Collecting data you do not need.
Shipping without a way to get crash reports.
Making no plan for updates after the first release.
whenToUpgrade: You need a backend of your own.
You need to meet company or regional compliance rules.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check store policies, data protection rules and every third-party licence before release.

title: Online store
headline: Your online store plan
example: I want to start an online store to sell products
starterBrief:
Goal: an online store that sells [products] to [customers].
How many products at the start: [number].
How I deliver: [courier, local, digital].
Payments I want: [UPI, cards, cash on delivery].
Rule: do not invent policies or prices; leave placeholders for me.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a launch checklist.

simple.summary: Use a store builder so catalogue, cart, checkout and hosting come in one place. Add ten products and test a real order.
simple.estimatedTime: A weekend to a week (rough estimate)

steps.title: List your first products
steps.detail: Write the name, one clear photo and a plain description for ten products.

steps.title: Write descriptions
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} to draft descriptions from facts you give it.
steps.examplePrompt: Write a short, honest product description from these facts only: [facts]. Do not add claims I did not give you.

steps.title: Set up the store
steps.detail: Create the shop in {job:website-builder} and add the products.

steps.title: Turn on payments
steps.detail: Connect {job:payments-india} and place a test order yourself.

commonMistakes: Launching with no clear delivery and return policy.
Using descriptions with claims you cannot back up.
whenToUpgrade: You need to show up in search.
You want product photos that look professional.
You want to sell to customers abroad.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check consumer, tax and delivery rules that apply to what you sell before you open.

polished.summary: Make the store look like a brand, photograph products well and make it findable in search and on social media.

steps.title: Fix the brand basics
steps.detail: Pick one logo, two colours and one font in {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Clean the product photos
steps.detail: Use {job:image-editing} for background and size, and keep photos consistent.

steps.title: Write for search
steps.detail: Use {job:seo} to find the words buyers type, and use them in titles and descriptions.

steps.title: Plan the first posts
steps.detail: Plan a month of posts with {job:social-media} and link them to products.

commonMistakes: Using different photo styles on every product.
whenToUpgrade: You track orders and customers by hand.
You need email and abandoned-cart reminders.
polished.checkTheFacts: Do not describe a product with a feature or certificate it does not have.

advanced.summary: Track the numbers, automate order messages and sell beyond one channel, with international payments if you ship abroad.

steps.title: Measure the funnel
steps.detail: Use {job:analytics} to see where visitors drop before checkout.

steps.title: Automate the boring parts
steps.detail: Use {job:automation-and-workflows} for order confirmations and stock alerts.

steps.title: Write the customer messages
steps.detail: Draft order, delay and return emails with {job:email-writing} and keep them kind and clear.

steps.title: Open to other countries
steps.detail: Add {job:payments-global} only after you know the shipping and tax rules.

commonMistakes: Changing many things at once so you cannot tell what worked.
Automating a message you never reread.
Selling abroad without a delivery plan.
whenToUpgrade: Orders outgrow a simple store builder.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check tax, import and consumer rules for every country you ship to.

title: Blog
headline: Your blog plan
example: I want to start a blog and write regularly
starterBrief:
Goal: a blog about [topic] for [readers].
How often I can post: [per week].
My experience with the topic: [short].
Rule: do not invent facts or quotes; mark anything you are unsure about.
Ask me anything you need, then give me ten post ideas and an outline for the first.

simple.summary: Start on a blogging platform, write one post a week with {job:ai-assistant} for outlines only, and publish the first post this week.
simple.estimatedTime: A day to set up, then weekly (rough estimate)

steps.title: Pick a topic you can keep up
steps.detail: Write the one thing your blog is about and who it helps.

steps.title: Outline the first post
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for an outline, then write the post in your own words.
steps.examplePrompt: Give me an outline for a 600-word post on [topic] for [reader]. Do not write the post.

steps.title: Edit it
steps.detail: Use {job:writing-and-editing} to fix grammar, then read it aloud once.

steps.title: Publish with {job:content-management}
steps.detail: Publish the post and share the link with three people.

commonMistakes: Starting with a perfect design and no posts.
Letting AI write everything so the posts sound like nobody.
whenToUpgrade: You want people to find the posts through search.
You want to know who reads them.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check every fact, name and quote in a post against its source before publishing.

polished.summary: Make posts easier to find with keyword research, add images and track what gets read.

steps.title: Find what people search for
steps.detail: Use {job:seo} to pick one clear phrase per post.

steps.title: Write and edit
steps.detail: Draft yourself, then use {job:writing-and-editing} to polish.

steps.title: Add a cover and diagrams
steps.detail: Make a simple cover with {job:image-generation} and label it if it is generated.

steps.title: Read the numbers
steps.detail: Use {job:analytics} monthly to see which posts are read and why.

commonMistakes: Using generated images that do not match the post.
whenToUpgrade: You want to earn from the blog.
You want a team of writers.
polished.checkTheFacts: Mark opinions as opinions, and link the sources you used.

advanced.summary: Run the blog like a publication: a content calendar, social sharing, and a newsletter to keep readers.

steps.title: Plan a quarter
steps.detail: Plan topics in a calendar with {job:social-media} and {job:seo} in mind.

steps.title: Collect emails
steps.detail: Add a signup with {job:contact-form}, and send a short note when you publish.

steps.title: Write the newsletter
steps.detail: Draft with {job:email-writing} and always add something not on the blog.

steps.title: Review monthly
steps.detail: Use {job:analytics} to drop what no one reads and double down on what they do.

commonMistakes: Collecting emails without saying how you will use them.
whenToUpgrade: You need legal pages and disclosures.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Disclose sponsored posts and affiliate links clearly.

title: Landing page
headline: Your landing page plan
example: I need a landing page for my product launch
starterBrief:
Goal: a landing page that gets [signups, sales, bookings] for [product or event].
Who it is for: [audience].
The one action I want: [action].
Proof I really have: [testimonials, numbers I can show].
Rule: do not invent testimonials or numbers.
Ask me anything you need, then give me the page sections and copy.

simple.summary: One page, one action: write the copy with {job:ai-assistant}, pick a template in {job:ui-templates} and publish on {job:hosting}.

steps.title: Name the one action
steps.detail: Choose the single thing visitors should do: sign up, buy or book.

steps.title: Write the copy
steps.detail: Ask {job:ai-assistant} for a headline, three benefits and a button label.
steps.examplePrompt: Write a landing page headline, three short benefits and a button label for [product] for [audience]. Use only facts I give: [facts].

steps.title: Pick a template
steps.detail: Choose a template in {job:ui-templates} and replace the text.

steps.title: Publish
steps.detail: Put it live with {job:hosting} and open it on your phone.

commonMistakes: Not checking the page on a phone.
whenToUpgrade: You want signups collected for you.
You want to know how many visitors act.
You want people to find the page in search.
simple.checkTheFacts: Show only real testimonials and numbers you can prove.

polished.summary: Collect signups, add a design that fits your brand and measure how many visitors act.

steps.title: Set the look
steps.detail: Pick two colours and one font in {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Add a signup
steps.detail: Collect signups with {job:contact-form} and say what you will send.

steps.title: Publish and measure
steps.detail: Put it live with {job:hosting} and count visits and signups in {job:analytics}.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.detail: Change only the headline, wait a week, and compare.

commonMistakes: Collecting emails with no plan to use them.
whenToUpgrade: You want people to find the page by search.
polished.checkTheFacts: Say how you will use the emails you collect, and let people unsubscribe.

advanced.summary: Code the page for speed, add payments and search basics, and keep an eye on how it performs.

steps.title: Build it lean
steps.detail: Build the page with {job:framework} and {job:component-library}, with no heavy scripts.

steps.title: Add payment
steps.detail: Add {job:payments-india} and test the full flow.

steps.title: Search basics
steps.detail: Use {job:seo} for title, description and headings.

steps.title: Measure and host
steps.detail: Deploy with {job:hosting} and track results with {job:analytics}.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Check consent rules and your payment provider's terms.

title: SaaS product
headline: Your SaaS plan
example: I want to build a SaaS product with subscriptions
starterBrief:
Goal: a SaaS product that helps [customer] do [job].
The problem in one sentence: [problem].
What I will charge for: [plan idea, no price needed yet].
What I can build myself: [skills].
Rule: be honest about what to validate before building.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a validation plan and a first-version scope.

simple.summary: Check that people want it before you build: talk to ten, make a clickable mock-up and a waitlist page.

steps.title: Write the problem
steps.detail: Describe who has the problem and how they solve it today.

steps.title: Talk to ten people
steps.detail: Ask about their current way, not your idea.
steps.examplePrompt: Write ten neutral questions to learn how [customer] handles [problem] today. Avoid mentioning my idea.

steps.title: Make a mock-up
steps.detail: Show the main screen in {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Collect a waitlist
steps.detail: Publish a page with {job:website-builder} and {job:contact-form}.

commonMistakes: Building for months before talking to a customer.
Asking friends who say yes to be nice.
Adding features before one customer pays.
whenToUpgrade: People ask when it is ready.
You need accounts and saved data.
simple.checkTheFacts: Do not count compliments as demand. Count people who commit time or money.

polished.summary: Build the smallest version with accounts and saved data, and charge early customers by hand.

steps.title: Cut the scope
steps.detail: List the one flow a paying customer needs and defer everything else.

steps.title: Build it
steps.detail: Build with {job:framework}, {job:database} and {job:authentication}, using {job:coding-assistant} for help.

steps.title: Host it
steps.detail: Put it online with {job:hosting}.

steps.title: Charge
steps.detail: Connect {job:payments-global} and charge the first customers directly.

commonMistakes: Building billing before you have users.
whenToUpgrade: Customers ask for more than one person per account.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check payment, tax and data protection rules for the places your customers live.

advanced.summary: Measure usage, protect customer data and automate the support and onboarding that eats your time.

steps.title: Track activation
steps.detail: Use {job:analytics} to see how many sign-ups reach the first value.

steps.title: Automate onboarding
steps.detail: Use {job:automation-and-workflows} for welcome and reminder emails.

steps.title: Protect it
steps.detail: Use {job:version-control} and write down who can access what in {job:database}.

steps.title: Review churn
steps.detail: Talk to every customer who leaves.

commonMistakes: No plan for incidents or backups.
Automating before you know the process.
whenToUpgrade: You sell to companies that ask about security.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Security and data promises must be true. Do not claim certifications you do not have.

title: Chatbot for my website
headline: Your website chatbot plan
example: I want a chatbot on my website to answer customer questions
starterBrief:
Goal: a chatbot on [website, WhatsApp] that answers [type of questions].
The information it may use: [FAQ, policies, product list].
What it must hand to a human: [refunds, complaints].
Rule: it must say when it does not know, and never invent policies or prices.
Ask me anything you need, then list the questions it must handle.

simple.summary: Start with a no-code chatbot builder, give it your FAQ and test it with your real questions before putting it live.

steps.title: Collect the questions
steps.detail: List the 20 questions customers ask most and the true answers.

steps.title: Build the bot
steps.detail: Create it in {job:chatbot-builder} using only your FAQ.

steps.title: Test it hard
steps.detail: Ask it questions it should not answer and make sure it says it does not know.
steps.examplePrompt: Write 15 tricky customer questions for a bot answering about [business], including ones it should refuse or hand to a person.

steps.title: Add a human handoff
steps.detail: Show an email or phone number for anything it cannot answer.

commonMistakes: Letting the bot invent prices or policies.
No way to reach a person.
whenToUpgrade: You want it on WhatsApp or other channels.
You want to see what people ask.
simple.checkTheFacts: A bot can answer wrongly with confidence. Review its answers against your real policies every week.

polished.summary: Add lead capture, a handoff to a human and a weekly review of what the bot got wrong.

steps.title: Capture leads
steps.detail: Add {job:contact-form} for people the bot cannot help.

steps.title: Review conversations
steps.detail: Read a sample of chats each week and fix gaps in the FAQ.

steps.title: Measure
steps.detail: Track how many chats end without help in {job:analytics}.

steps.title: Say it is a bot
steps.detail: Tell visitors they are talking to an automated assistant.

commonMistakes: Hiding that it is a bot.
Storing chats with personal data without a reason.
whenToUpgrade: Questions need your own data or documents.

polished.summary: Add your own art and sound, a simple menu and a place people can play it.

steps.detail: Use {job:image-generation} for concept art and edit it to fit.

steps.detail: Host a web build on {job:hosting} and share the link.

polished.summary: Use a dashboard tool connected to your data, refresh automatically and share a link.

steps.title: Refresh it
steps.detail: Schedule updates with {job:automation-and-workflows}.

steps.detail: Create tables in {job:database} and load a copy of the source.

steps.detail: Use {job:framework} with {job:coding-assistant}.

steps.title: Test the numbers
steps.detail: Write a few tests that compare totals with known values.

simple.summary: Write the steps by hand first. Then connect two apps with a no-code tool, and let it ask for your approval at the end.

steps.detail: Make it send you a draft first, not act on its own.

simple.checkTheFacts: Check what data passes through each connected app, and what each app is allowed to do.

polished.summary: Add AI steps for sorting and drafting, error alerts and a log of what ran.

steps.title: Add a drafting step
steps.detail: Let {job:ai-assistant} draft replies or summaries, and keep a human check.

steps.title: Log everything
steps.detail: Write each run to a sheet with {job:spreadsheet-ai}.

steps.title: Alert on failure
steps.detail: Get a message when a step fails.

advanced.summary: Write custom scripts for what no-code tools cannot do, in version control, with tests and secrets stored safely.

steps.detail: Use {job:seo} to see what viewers search for before you title.
