title: Personal productivity
headline: Your productivity plan
example: I want to organise my work and be more productive every day
synonyms: notes and tasks in one place
starterBrief:
Goal: a simple system to manage [work, study, life].
What I keep forgetting: [list].
How many tasks I handle a week: [number].
Tools I already use: [list].
Rule: keep it simple enough to use on a bad day.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a daily and weekly routine.

simple.summary: One list, one calendar. Write every task in one place, pick three for today and review each evening.
simple.estimatedTime: A day to set up (rough estimate)

steps.title: Dump everything
steps.detail: Write all tasks and commitments in one list in {job:task-and-project-management}.

steps.title: Pick three
steps.detail: Choose three tasks for today, and put them in your calendar.

steps.title: Keep notes together
steps.detail: Use {job:note-taking} for notes, linked to tasks.

steps.title: Review each evening
steps.detail: Spend five minutes: what is done, what moves, what is next.

commonMistakes: Planning too many tasks per day.
simple.checkTheFacts: A system you stop using is worse than a simple one. Start smaller if it feels heavy.

polished.summary: Add a weekly review, templates for repeating work and a calm inbox routine.

steps.title: Weekly review
steps.detail: Every Sunday: clear the list, plan the week, and cancel the rest.

steps.title: Templates
steps.detail: Make templates for repeated tasks in {job:note-taking}.

steps.title: Inbox routine
steps.detail: Check mail twice a day and draft replies with {job:email-writing}.

steps.title: Automate one thing
steps.detail: Use {job:automation-and-workflows} for one repeating task.

whenToUpgrade: Your tools do not talk to each other.
polished.checkTheFacts: Do not let an automation send messages in your name without a check.

advanced.summary: Connect your tools, plan projects in phases and review monthly goals with data.

steps.title: Plan by project
steps.detail: Break each project into phases with dates.

steps.title: Connect tools
steps.detail: Use {job:automation-and-workflows} to send tasks between apps.

steps.title: Track your time
steps.detail: Log where hours go in {job:spreadsheet-ai} for two weeks.

steps.title: Review monthly
steps.detail: Cut what takes time and gives nothing.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Check what data each connected app can read before linking it.

title: Music creation
headline: Your music plan
example: I want to make a song or background music
starterBrief:
Goal: a [song, instrumental, jingle] for [use] in the style of [genre, mood].
Length: [seconds].
Lyrics or theme: [short].
Where I will use it: [video, reel, podcast].
Rule: no copying of existing songs or artists.
Ask me anything you need, then write lyrics or a prompt for the music tool.

simple.summary: Describe the mood and length, generate a few options in a music tool and pick one that fits.

steps.title: Describe the mood
steps.detail: Write genre, mood, tempo and where you will use it.

steps.title: Generate options
steps.detail: Try three prompts in {job:music-generation} and listen to each.
steps.examplePrompt: Write three prompts for an AI music tool for [use], [mood], [length], without naming any artist or song.

steps.title: Pick one
steps.detail: Choose the one that fits your video or project, not the flashiest.

steps.title: Check the terms
steps.detail: Read the tool's licence for commercial use before publishing.

commonMistakes: Naming a real artist in the prompt.
whenToUpgrade: You need it for a video.
simple.checkTheFacts: Licence terms for AI-generated music differ by tool and plan. Read them before monetising.

polished.summary: Write lyrics yourself, shape the arrangement and clean the audio.

steps.title: Write the lyrics
steps.detail: Draft in your own words and use {job:ai-assistant} to rhyme and tighten.

steps.title: Generate and compare
steps.detail: Make several versions in {job:music-generation}.

steps.title: Clean and mix
steps.detail: Use {job:voice-and-audio} to remove noise and balance volume.

steps.title: Make cover art
steps.detail: Create a cover in {job:design-tool}.

commonMistakes: Lyrics that mimic a known song.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check that lyrics and melody are not too close to an existing song.

advanced.summary: Produce with a digital audio workstation, record real vocals or instruments and release properly.

steps.title: Build the track
steps.detail: Combine generated parts with your own recordings.

steps.title: Mix and master
steps.detail: Balance levels with {job:voice-and-audio} and test on speakers and earphones.

steps.title: Make a video
steps.detail: Cut a lyric video in {job:video-editing}.

steps.title: Release
steps.detail: Check distributor rules and credit everything.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Check your distributor's policy on AI-generated music and rights.

title: Edit a video
headline: Your video editing plan
example: I have raw footage and want to edit it into a good video
starterBrief:
Goal: edit [footage] into a [length] video for [platform].
What I have: [clips, audio, music].
The story or message: [one sentence].
Style: [fast cuts, calm, documentary].
Rule: only use music and clips I have the right to use.
Ask me anything you need, then give me an edit plan with timings.

simple.summary: Pick a simple editor, cut the best parts, fix the sound and add captions.

steps.title: Write the story
steps.detail: In one sentence: what should a viewer feel or learn?

steps.title: Rough cut
steps.detail: Drop the clips in {job:video-editing} and delete everything that does not serve the sentence.

steps.title: Fix the sound
steps.detail: Clean the audio. Poor sound loses viewers faster than a poor picture.

steps.title: Add captions
steps.detail: Generate captions and fix the mistakes by hand.
steps.examplePrompt: Here is my caption text: [text]. Fix spelling and punctuation only, and do not change the meaning or words.

whenToUpgrade: You want cleaner audio and music.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check that you have the right to use every clip and track in the video.

polished.summary: Add sound design, a consistent look and a thumbnail, and export for the right platform.

steps.title: Clean and balance the audio
steps.detail: Use {job:voice-and-audio} to remove noise and level the voices.

steps.title: Add music
steps.detail: Create or choose music with {job:music-generation} and keep it under the voice.

steps.title: Create captions
steps.detail: Use {job:meeting-notes-and-transcription} for text, then fix errors.

steps.title: Make a thumbnail and export
steps.detail: Design in {job:design-tool} and export at the platform's recommended size.

whenToUpgrade: You want AI clips or effects.
polished.checkTheFacts: Disclose generated voices, clips or music where the platform asks.

advanced.summary: Build a repeatable workflow: templates, proxy edits, colour work and a review process.

steps.title: Create templates
steps.detail: Save intro, lower-thirds and caption styles.

steps.title: Use generated clips sparingly
steps.detail: Use {job:video-generation} only for b-roll and label it.

steps.title: Track versions
steps.detail: Name and date every export in {job:task-and-project-management}.

steps.title: Review
steps.detail: Watch on a phone with and without sound.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Check licences for fonts, music and footage before delivery.

title: Edit photos and images
headline: Your image editing plan
example: I want to edit photos and remove the background
starterBrief:
Goal: edit [photos] so that [result].
How many images: [number].
Where they will be used: [website, print, social].
Size or format needed: [pixels, ratio, file size].
Rule: do not change the facts in a photo that will be used as evidence or news.
Ask me anything you need, then give me the steps for one photo first.

simple.summary: Use a simple editor in your browser: crop, fix light, remove the background and export at the right size.

steps.title: Decide the use
steps.detail: Website, print and social have different sizes.

steps.title: Do the basic fixes
steps.detail: Crop, straighten and fix brightness in {job:image-editing}.

steps.title: Remove the background
steps.detail: Try the one-click remover and check the edges.

steps.title: Export
steps.detail: Save a copy, keep the original, and check the file size.

commonMistakes: Wrong file size for the use.
simple.checkTheFacts: Do not alter a photo in a way that misleads viewers, and label edited or generated images where it matters.

polished.summary: Add consistent colour, batch work and designs around the photos.

steps.title: Set one look
steps.detail: Use the same colour and crop style for a set.

steps.title: Batch process
steps.detail: Apply the same fixes to many photos in {job:image-editing}.

steps.title: Design with them
steps.detail: Place photos in posters or banners with {job:design-tool}.

steps.title: Fill gaps
steps.detail: Use {job:stock-assets} or {job:image-generation} and check licences.

polished.checkTheFacts: Check licences and releases for any image of a person or a place.

advanced.summary: Work non-destructively with layers, colour profiles and an automated pipeline for volume.

steps.title: Use layers and masks
steps.detail: Keep each edit reversible.

steps.title: Manage colour
steps.detail: Work in one colour profile, and test on a print proof.

steps.title: Automate
steps.detail: Use {job:automation-and-workflows} to resize and rename big batches.

steps.title: Keep an archive
steps.detail: Store originals and edits separately, with notes.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Keep records of model and property releases.

title: 3D models
headline: Your 3D plan
example: I want to create a 3D model for printing or a website
starterBrief:
Goal: a 3D [model, scene, animation] of [thing] for [web, print, game, video].
Size and detail needed: [low, medium, high].
My experience: [none, some].
Rule: tell me which parts are easy for a beginner and which are not.
Ask me anything you need, then give me a step-by-step build.

simple.summary: Start with a browser-based 3D tool, model a simple object, and export it.

steps.title: Choose one simple object
steps.detail: A mug, a logo or a chair. Not a character.

steps.title: Follow a beginner tutorial
steps.detail: Use {job:3d-and-design-assets} and one tutorial from start to finish.

steps.title: Model it
steps.detail: Build with simple shapes and keep it low detail.
steps.examplePrompt: I am a beginner making a simple [object] in [tool]. Give me the steps in order and what each tool does.

steps.title: Export and check
steps.detail: Export in the format you need and open it somewhere else.

whenToUpgrade: You want it on a website.
simple.checkTheFacts: For printing, check size, wall thickness and the printer's limits before you print.

polished.summary: Add materials, lighting and rendering, and use free assets where it saves time.

steps.title: Collect assets
steps.detail: Use free models and textures from {job:stock-assets} and note their licences.

steps.title: Set materials and light
steps.detail: Keep lighting simple: one key light and one fill.

steps.title: Render
steps.detail: Render still images or a short turntable.

steps.title: Edit the result
steps.detail: Cut an animation in {job:video-editing}.

commonMistakes: Rendering at huge size by default.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check licences of assets before commercial use.

advanced.summary: Put 3D on the web or in a game, with optimised models and a build pipeline.

steps.title: Optimise
steps.detail: Reduce polygons and texture sizes.

steps.title: Load in the web
steps.detail: Use {job:framework} and {job:animation-library} to show the model.

steps.title: Host
steps.detail: Put files on {job:hosting} and test on mobile.

steps.title: Version it
steps.detail: Keep source files in {job:version-control}.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Test on a mid-range phone, not only your machine.

title: Analyse data in spreadsheets
headline: Your spreadsheet analysis plan
example: I want to analyse my data in Excel or Google Sheets
starterBrief:
Goal: analyse [data] in [Excel, Google Sheets] to answer [question].
Columns I have: [list].
How many rows: [number].
What the answer should look like: [table, chart, number].
Rule: show me the formula and explain it, and do not make up values.
Ask me anything you need, then give me the steps.

simple.summary: Clean the data, ask {job:ai-assistant} for the formula you need, and test it on a few rows first.

steps.title: Look at the data
steps.detail: Check headers, blanks, dates and duplicates.

steps.title: Say what you need
steps.detail: Describe columns and the result you want.
steps.examplePrompt: My sheet has columns A: [name], B: [name]... I need a formula in [Excel, Google Sheets] that [goal]. Give the formula and explain it in one line.

steps.title: Test on five rows
steps.detail: Check the formula by hand before filling it down.

steps.title: Save a copy
steps.detail: Keep the original data untouched.

commonMistakes: Trusting a formula you did not test.
Mixed data types in a column.
simple.checkTheFacts: Check totals against a hand calculation. A wrong formula looks right.

polished.summary: Use pivot tables and charts to answer your questions, and document each step.

steps.title: Build a pivot table
steps.detail: Summarise by the group you care about.

steps.title: Chart it
steps.detail: Use {job:data-analysis} to choose one chart per question.

steps.title: Write the findings
steps.detail: Use {job:writing-and-editing} for three plain sentences.

steps.title: Note your steps
steps.detail: Write how you cleaned and calculated.

polished.checkTheFacts: Say what the data does not show. Do not claim cause from a simple pattern.

advanced.summary: Automate with scripts and move to code when sheets are too slow, with checks at each step.

steps.title: Script the cleaning
steps.detail: Ask {job:coding-assistant} for a script that does your cleaning steps.

steps.title: Move large data
steps.detail: Store it in {job:database}.

steps.title: Schedule
steps.detail: Use {job:automation-and-workflows} to refresh.

steps.title: Add checks
steps.detail: Compare totals with the source after each run.

commonMistakes: Changing the source file by hand.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Keep a record of every transformation so a result can be reproduced.

title: Build an AI agent
headline: Your AI agent plan
example: I want to build an AI agent that can do tasks for me
starterBrief:
Goal: an AI agent that [does what] using [tools or data].
What it may do on its own: [list].
What needs my approval: [list].
What it must never do: [list].
Rule: design for mistakes: logs, limits and a way to stop it.
Ask me anything you need, then give me the tools, steps and tests.

simple.summary: Start without code: one task, a few tools in a visual builder, and a human approval step.

steps.title: Pick one task
steps.detail: One narrow task with clear success, such as sorting emails.

steps.title: List allowed actions
steps.detail: Write what it may do, and what needs your approval.

steps.title: Build in {job:automation-and-workflows}
steps.detail: Connect the tools with a visual flow.
steps.examplePrompt: Help me design an AI workflow for [task]. List the steps, the input of each, and where a human must approve.

steps.title: Test with bad input
steps.detail: Try empty, long and tricky inputs.

simple.checkTheFacts: An agent can take wrong actions with confidence. Limit what it can do and review what it did.

polished.summary: Write a small agent in code with tools, tests and logs, and keep a human in the loop for risky actions.

steps.title: Define tools
steps.detail: Each tool does one thing with clear inputs.

steps.title: Write the loop
steps.detail: Use {job:coding-assistant} for the agent loop and limits.
steps.examplePrompt: Write a minimal agent loop in [language] with [tools], a step limit, and logging of every tool call.

steps.title: Add memory
steps.detail: Store what it needs in {job:database}.

steps.title: Test and log
steps.detail: Save every run and replay failures.

polished.checkTheFacts: Test with adversarial inputs, including instructions hidden in documents or web pages.

advanced.summary: Add evaluation, authentication, permissions and monitoring, and consider running models yourself.

steps.title: Write an evaluation set
steps.detail: A list of tasks with expected outcomes, rerun after each change.

steps.title: Permission each tool
steps.detail: Use {job:authentication} and scope every tool.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.detail: Track cost, errors and unusual actions with {job:analytics}.

steps.title: Choose the model location
steps.detail: Use {job:run-ai-locally} where privacy requires it.

whenToUpgrade: It acts on money or data.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Prompt injection and data leaks are real risks. Do not give an agent more access than it needs.

title: Local private AI
headline: Your private AI plan
example: I want to run AI on my own computer without sending data online
starterBrief:
Goal: run AI privately on [my laptop, a server] for [tasks].
My computer: [RAM, graphics card, or not sure].
What data must stay private: [types].
What I want it to do: [chat, summarise, code].
Rule: be honest about speed and quality limits on my hardware.
Ask me anything you need, then recommend model sizes and a setup order.

simple.summary: Install a desktop app that runs small models, pick a small model that fits your memory and test it on a harmless task first.

steps.title: Check your computer
steps.detail: Note your RAM and whether you have a graphics card. It decides model size.

steps.title: Install a runner
steps.detail: Use {job:run-ai-locally} to install a desktop app and download one small model.

steps.title: Try a harmless task
steps.detail: Ask it to summarise a public article and notice speed and quality.
steps.examplePrompt: Summarise this text in five bullet points and list anything you are not sure about: [text]

steps.title: Decide what to keep local
steps.detail: Move private tasks here only if quality is good enough.

commonMistakes: Downloading a model too big for your memory.
Expecting the quality of the biggest cloud tools.
whenToUpgrade: You want to chat with your files.
You want to use it from other devices.
simple.checkTheFacts: Download models only from official sources and check their licences. Local models can be wrong too.

polished.summary: Add document chat on your own files, a web interface and a few models for different jobs.

steps.title: Pick models by job
steps.detail: A small fast model for drafts, a larger one for harder questions.

steps.title: Chat with files
steps.detail: Index your files with {job:pdf-and-document-chat} and check quoted passages.

steps.title: Add an interface
steps.detail: Use {job:chatbot-builder} for a friendly local web page.

steps.title: Test your files
steps.detail: Ask ten questions you know the answers to.

commonMistakes: Exposing the interface to the internet.
whenToUpgrade: You share it with a team.
polished.checkTheFacts: Check your local setup for open network ports before sharing a machine.

advanced.summary: Serve models for a team with access control, monitoring and a plan for updates.

steps.title: Choose the hardware
steps.detail: Match memory and graphics to the models you will serve.

steps.title: Control access
steps.detail: Use {job:authentication} so only your team can use it.

steps.title: Log and limit
steps.detail: Record usage and set limits.

steps.title: Plan updates
steps.detail: Pin model versions and test before changing.

advanced.checkTheFacts: Review licences and security of every model and tool you run.

title: Plan built from your parts
headline: Your custom plan
example: A plan built from the parts I describe
starterBrief:
Goal: [what I want to achieve].
The parts I need: [list].
Who it is for: [audience].
What I already have: [tools, files, skills].
Rule: use only facts I give you, and say what you are unsure about.
Ask me anything you need, then give me the order to do the parts in.

simple.summary: Work through the parts in order: idea first, then design, build, data, payments, launch and growth. Do one part at a time and check it.

steps.title: Write the goal in one sentence
steps.detail: Say who it is for and what done looks like.

steps.title: Start with the idea
steps.detail: Use {job:ai-assistant} to turn your sentence into a short list of what must exist.

steps.title: Do the parts in order
steps.detail: Work down the cards. Finish one part before starting the next.

steps.title: Check each part
steps.detail: Test the part on a small real example before you move on.

commonMistakes: Paying for tools before you have tried the free options.
Trusting the first answer without checking.
whenToUpgrade: A part turns out bigger than expected.
Two parts need to work together.
You want a plan that matches a common goal.
simple.checkTheFacts: AI output can be wrong or invented. Check anything that matters against the original or a trusted source.

polished.summary: Add design and structure: decide how the parts connect, and write down the data that moves between them.

steps.title: Draw how the parts connect
steps.detail: A box for each part and an arrow for what passes between them.

steps.title: Choose tools that work together
steps.detail: Prefer tools that list each other as compatible, and read each card's note.

steps.title: Build in small steps
steps.detail: Finish one part end to end before the next.

steps.title: Write it down
steps.detail: Keep a short note of what you chose and why.

commonMistakes: Tools that do not fit each other.
No notes, so you cannot repeat it.
whenToUpgrade: The plan has more than six parts.
You need others to use it.
You need it to be reliable.
polished.checkTheFacts: AI output can be wrong or invented. Check anything that matters against the original or a trusted source.

advanced.summary: Treat it as a project: version everything, test each part, protect data and measure what happens after launch.

steps.title: Set up a project space
steps.detail: Keep files, notes and decisions in one place with history.

steps.title: Test each part and the whole
steps.detail: Write a short checklist for what must work.

steps.title: Protect data and keys
steps.detail: Keep secrets out of files you share.

steps.title: Launch small and measure
steps.detail: Release to a few people and look at what they do.

commonMistakes: Launching with no way to fix problems.
advanced.checkTheFacts: Check legal, privacy and platform rules that apply to what you build.
